surviving_claim: In the tested single-writer process-crash model, a fixed-page committed epoch can coordinate persistent exact SQLite overflow without contaminating successful common-path lookup. Durable future rows remain hidden until coordinator commit, indexed startup cleanup prevents abandoned-row resurrection, and stale fixed-page suffixes can be truncated to the committed next_page_id frontier with zero application logical redo.
negative_result: The stale uncommitted file-length range created by eager generation allocation is 4096*(C+2)=Theta(C). One ftruncate call therefore does not establish constant reclamation volume or device work.
non_claims: the recovery procedure itself has not yet been interrupted by SIGKILL at internal cleanup boundaries
the stale-tail byte range is file length; filesystem allocated-block reclamation and device work are not measured
SQLite internal WAL-frame and fsync counts are not measured by the wrapper-level logical commit count
overflow lookup remains a comparison-B-tree path whose height grows with overflow cardinality
the tested process-crash protocol does not establish arbitrary hardware power-loss or torn-write behavior
no multi-writer, distributed-consistency, production-latency, throughput, or cost claim
